delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retain the cloud-darkness image introducing Solomon’s response.
verses.before: Then Solomon said: “The LORD said that he would dwell in thick darkness.
verses.after: Then Solomon said, “The LORD said he would dwell in thick darkness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Solomon said: “The LORD said that he would dwell in thick darkness.

verses.rationale: Keep the paired dwelling lines and permanent claim as poetry.
verses.before: Yet I have built you an exalted house, a place for you to dwell forever.”
verses.after: I have built you a lofty house, a settled place for you to dwell forever.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But I have built you an exalted house, a place for you to dwell forever.”

verses.rationale: Clarify the king’s turn toward the assembled people.
verses.before: Then the king turned his face and blessed all the assembly of Israel, while all the assembly of Israel stood.
verses.after: The king turned toward the whole assembly of Israel and blessed them. Everyone remained standing.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king turned his face and blessed all the assembly of Israel, while all the assembly of Israel stood.

verses.rationale: Preserve mouth and hands linking promise and fulfillment.
verses.before: He said, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth to David my father and fulfilled it with his hands, saying,
verses.after: He said, “Blessed be the LORD, Israel’s God! With his own hands he has fulfilled what his own mouth promised my father David:
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth to David my father and fulfilled it with his hands, saying,

verses.rationale: Retain both negative choices before their positive counterparts.
verses.before: ‘From the day I brought my people out from the land of Egypt, I did not choose a city from all the tribes of Israel to build a house so that my name might be there, and I did not choose a man to be ruler over my people Israel.
verses.after: ‘From the day I brought my people out of Egypt, I chose no city among all Israel’s tribes for a house where my name would dwell, and I chose no one to lead my people Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘From the day I brought my people out from the land of Egypt, I did not choose a city from all the tribes of Israel to build a house so that my name might be there, and I did not choose a man to be ruler over my people Israel.

verses.rationale: Repeat chose and name to carry the contrast.
verses.before: Yet I have chosen Jerusalem so that my name may be there, and I have chosen David to be over my people Israel.’
verses.after: But I chose Jerusalem for my name to dwell there, and I chose David to lead my people Israel.’
verses.tsw_comparator: But I have chosen Jerusalem so that my name may be there, and I have chosen David to be over my people Israel.’

verses.rationale: Keep heart and name central to the building intention.
verses.before: It was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.after: “My father David had it in his heart to build a house for the name of the LORD, Israel’s God.
verses.tsw_comparator: It was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

verses.rationale: Distinguish approval of intention from permission to build.
verses.before: But the LORD said to David my father, ‘Because it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart.
verses.after: But the LORD told my father David, ‘You did well to have it in your heart to build a house for my name.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD said to David my father, ‘Because it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart.

verses.rationale: Clarify bodily descent while retaining the prohibition.
verses.before: Even so, you will not build the house, but your son who comes from your body—he will build the house for my name.’
verses.after: Even so, you will not build the house. Your son, born from your own body, will build the house for my name.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Nevertheless, you shall not build the house, but your son who comes from your body—he shall build the house for my name.’

verses.rationale: Connect succession and construction with the fulfilled promise.
verses.before: The LORD has established his word that he spoke, for I have risen in place of David my father and sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD spoke, and I have built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.after: “The LORD has fulfilled his promise. I have succeeded my father David and taken Israel’s throne, just as the LORD said, and I have built the house for the name of the LORD, Israel’s God.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has established his word that he spoke, for I have risen in place of David my father and sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD spoke, and I have built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserve covenant as the ark’s contents without inserting tablets.
verses.before: There I have placed the ark in which is the covenant of the LORD that he made with the children of Israel.”
verses.after: I have placed the ark there. In it is the LORD’s covenant, which he made with the Israelites.”
verses.tsw_comparator: There I have placed the ark in which is the covenant of the LORD that he made with the children of Israel.”

verses.rationale: Name Solomon at the return to narration.
verses.before: Then he stood before the altar of the LORD in the presence of all the assembly of Israel and spread out his hands.
verses.after: Solomon stood before the LORD’s altar, facing the whole assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he stood before the altar of the LORD in the presence of all the assembly of Israel and spread out his hands.

verses.rationale: Keep every dimension and the change from standing to kneeling.
verses.before: For Solomon had made a bronze platform, five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high, and had put it among the court. He stood upon it, knelt on his knees before all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands toward the heavens.
verses.after: He had made a bronze platform five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high and set it in the middle of the courtyard. He stood on it, then knelt before the whole assembly of Israel and spread his hands toward heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Solomon had made a bronze platform, five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high, and had put it in the midst of the court. He stood upon it, knelt on his knees before all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands toward the heavens.

verses.rationale: Retain covenant, faithful love and wholehearted walking.
verses.before: He said: “O LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you in the heavens or on the earth, keeping covenant and steadfast love with your servants who walk before you with all their heart.
verses.after: He prayed, “LORD, Israel’s God, there is no God like you in heaven or on earth. You keep covenant and faithful love with your servants who walk before you with all their heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said: “O LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you in the heavens or on the earth, keeping covenant and steadfast love with your servants who walk before you with all their heart.

verses.rationale: Repeat the embodied promise-and-fulfillment language.
verses.before: You have kept with your servant David my father what you spoke to him. You spoke with your mouth and with your hand have fulfilled it this day.
verses.after: You have kept the promise you made to your servant David my father. What you spoke with your mouth you have fulfilled with your hand, as we see today.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have kept with your servant David my father what you spoke to him. You spoke with your mouth and with your hand have fulfilled it this day.

verses.rationale: Make the condition audible without weakening the royal promise.
verses.before: And now, O LORD, God of Israel, keep with your servant David my father what you spoke to him, saying, ‘There will not be cut off from you a man before me to sit upon the throne of Israel, if only your sons guard their way, to walk in my instruction as you have walked before me.’
verses.after: Now, LORD, Israel’s God, keep this promise you made to your servant David my father: ‘You will never lack a man to sit before me on Israel’s throne, provided your sons watch their ways and walk in my instruction as you have walked before me.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, O LORD, God of Israel, keep with your servant David my father what you spoke to him, saying, ‘There shall not be cut off from you a man before me to sit upon the throne of Israel, if only your sons guard their way, to walk in my instruction as you have walked before me.’

verses.rationale: Maintain the request that the promise be confirmed.
verses.before: And now, O LORD, God of Israel, let your word be confirmed that you spoke to your servant David.
verses.after: Now, LORD, Israel’s God, let the word you spoke to your servant David prove true.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, O LORD, God of Israel, let your word be confirmed that you spoke to your servant David.

verses.rationale: Retain the question and its escalating contrast.
verses.before: “But will God truly dwell with humanity upon the earth? Look, the heavens and the highest heavens cannot contain you; how much less this house that I have built!
verses.after: “But will God really dwell with human beings on earth? Heaven, even the highest heavens, cannot contain you! How much less this house I have built!
verses.tsw_comparator: “But will God truly dwell with humanity upon the earth? Look, the heavens and the highest heavens cannot contain you; how much less this house that I have built!

verses.rationale: Carry the appeal from transcendence to attentive hearing.
verses.before: Yet turn toward the prayer of your servant and toward his plea, O LORD my God, to hear the cry and the prayer that your servant prays before you,
verses.after: Yet attend to your servant’s prayer and plea, LORD my God. Listen to the cry and the prayer your servant offers before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet turn toward the prayer of your servant and toward his plea, O LORD my God, to hear the cry and the prayer that your servant prays before you,

verses.rationale: Preserve eyes, name and directional prayer.
verses.before: that your eyes may be open toward this house day and night, toward the place of which you said that you would put your name there, to hear the prayer that your servant prays toward this place.
verses.after: May your eyes be open toward this house day and night, toward the place where you said you would put your name. Hear the prayer your servant offers toward this place.
verses.tsw_comparator: that your eyes may be open toward this house day and night, toward the place of which you said that you would put your name there, to hear the prayer that your servant prays toward this place.

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated hearing and short climactic petition.
verses.before: Hear the pleas of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from your dwelling place, from the heavens; hear and forgive.
verses.after: Hear the pleas your servant and your people Israel offer toward this place. Hear from heaven, your dwelling place. Hear, and forgive.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear the pleas of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from your dwelling place, from the heavens; hear and forgive.

verses.rationale: Leave the oath’s courtroom function without inventing an ordeal.
verses.before: “If a man sins against his neighbor and an oath is laid upon him to make him swear, and the oath comes before your altar in this house,
verses.after: “When someone wrongs a neighbor and is required to swear an oath, and the oath is brought before your altar in this house,
verses.tsw_comparator: “If a man sins against his neighbor and an oath is laid upon him to make him swear, and the oath comes before your altar in this house,

verses.rationale: Preserve judicial contrast and the head image with generic referents.
verses.before: then hear from the heavens and act. Judge your servants, repaying the wicked by bringing his way upon his head and declaring the righteous righteous by giving him according to his righteousness.
verses.after: hear from heaven and act. Judge between your servants: repay the guilty by bringing their conduct down on their own heads, and vindicate the righteous by treating them according to their righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: then hear from the heavens and act. Judge your servants, repaying the wicked by bringing his way upon his head and declaring the righteous righteous by giving him according to his righteousness.

verses.rationale: Retain the stated cause and the successive acts of return.
verses.before: “When your people Israel are struck before an enemy because they sinned against you, and they return and confess your name and pray and plead before you in this house,
verses.after: “When your people Israel are defeated by an enemy because they have sinned against you, and they turn back, acknowledge your name, and pray and plead before you in this house,
verses.tsw_comparator: “When your people Israel are struck before an enemy because they sinned against you, and they return and confess your name and pray and plead before you in this house,

verses.rationale: Keep forgiveness and return to ancestral ground together.
verses.before: then hear from the heavens and forgive the sin of your people Israel and bring them back to the ground that you gave to them and to their ancestors.
verses.after: hear from heaven. Forgive the sin of your people Israel and bring them back to the ground you gave them and their ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: then hear from the heavens and forgive the sin of your people Israel and bring them back to the ground that you gave to them and to their ancestors.

verses.rationale: Preserve the shut-heaven image and the attribution of affliction.
verses.before: “When the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because they sinned against you, and they pray toward this place and confess your name and turn from their sin because you humble them,
verses.after: “When the heavens are shut and no rain falls because they have sinned against you, and they pray toward this place, acknowledge your name, and turn from their sin because you have afflicted them,
verses.tsw_comparator: “When the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because they sinned against you, and they pray toward this place and confess your name and turn from their sin because you humble them,

verses.rationale: Retain instruction, walking and inherited land.
verses.before: then hear in the heavens and forgive the sin of your servants and your people Israel, when you teach them the good way in which they should walk. Give rain upon your land that you gave to your people as an inheritance.
verses.after: hear from heaven. Forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel, as you teach them the good way to walk. Send rain on the land you gave your people as their inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: then hear in the heavens and forgive the sin of your servants and your people Israel, when you teach them the good way in which they should walk. Give rain upon your land that you gave to your people as an inheritance.

verses.rationale: Keep the full disaster list and siege setting.
verses.before: “If there is famine in the land, if there is plague, blight, mildew, locust, or grasshopper; if their enemies besiege them in the land at their gates; whatever plague or sickness there may be—
verses.after: “When famine strikes the land, or plague, blight, mildew, locusts or devouring locusts; when enemies besiege them in the land at their gates; whatever the affliction or disease,
verses.tsw_comparator: “If there is famine in the land, if there is plague, blight, mildew, locust, or grasshopper; if their enemies besiege them in the land at their gates; whatever plague or sickness there may be—

verses.rationale: Keep personal pain within the communal petition.
verses.before: whatever prayer, whatever plea is made by any person or by all your people Israel, each knowing his own affliction and pain and spreading out his hands toward this house—
verses.after: whatever prayer or plea any person or all your people Israel offer, each knowing their own affliction and pain and spreading their hands toward this house,
verses.tsw_comparator: whatever prayer, whatever plea is made by any person or by all your people Israel, each knowing his own affliction and pain and spreading out his hands toward this house—

verses.rationale: Preserve the exclusive knowledge of hearts and individual response.
verses.before: then hear from the heavens, your dwelling place, and forgive. Give to each according to all his ways, for you know his heart—for you alone know the heart of the children of humanity—
verses.after: hear from heaven, your settled dwelling place, and forgive. Deal with each according to all their ways, for you know their heart—you alone know the hearts of human beings—
verses.tsw_comparator: then hear from the heavens, your dwelling place, and forgive. Give to each according to all his ways, for you know his heart—for you alone know the heart of the children of humanity—

verses.rationale: Connect reverence and conduct to the preceding request.
verses.before: so that they may fear you and walk in your ways all the days that they live upon the face of the ground that you gave to our ancestors.
verses.after: so that they may fear you and walk in your ways all the days they live on the ground you gave our ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that they may fear you and walk in your ways all the days that they live upon the face of the ground that you gave to our ancestors.

verses.rationale: Use inclusive foreigners while retaining the distinct non-Israelite referent.
verses.before: “And also concerning the foreigner who is not from your people Israel, when he comes from a distant land because of your great name, your strong hand, and your outstretched arm, and he comes and prays toward this house,
verses.after: “As for foreigners who do not belong to your people Israel but come from a distant land because of your great name, your strong hand, and your outstretched arm: when they come and pray toward this house,
verses.tsw_comparator: “And also concerning the foreigner who is not from your people Israel, when he comes from a distant land because of your great name, your strong hand, and your outstretched arm, and he comes and prays toward this house,

verses.rationale: Preserve the expansive request and the repeated name motif.
verses.before: then hear from the heavens, from your dwelling place, and do according to all for which the foreigner calls to you, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, as your people Israel do, and know that your name is called upon this house that I have built.
verses.after: hear from heaven, your settled dwelling place. Do all the foreigner calls on you to do, so that all earth’s peoples may know your name and fear you as your people Israel do, and know that this house I have built bears your name.
verses.tsw_comparator: then hear from the heavens, from your dwelling place, and do according to all for which the foreigner calls to you, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, as your people Israel do, and know that your name is called upon this house that I have built.

verses.rationale: Keep the stated divine sending and direction of prayer.
verses.before: “When your people go out to battle against their enemies by the way you send them, and they pray to you toward this city that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name,
verses.after: “When your people go to war against their enemies by whatever route you send them, and pray to you toward this city you have chosen and the house I have built for your name,
verses.tsw_comparator: “When your people go out to battle against their enemies by the way you send them, and they pray to you toward this city that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name,

verses.rationale: Retain the legal sense of doing their justice.
verses.before: then hear from the heavens their prayer and their plea and maintain their cause.
verses.after: hear their prayer and plea from heaven, and uphold their cause.
verses.tsw_comparator: then hear from the heavens their prayer and their plea and maintain their cause.

verses.rationale: Preserve universal sin and the concrete captivity sequence.
verses.before: “When they sin against you—for there is no human being who does not sin—and you become angry with them and give them before an enemy, and their captors carry them captive to a land far or near,
verses.after: “When they sin against you—for there is no one who does not sin—and you are angry with them and hand them over to an enemy, so that their captors take them to a land far away or nearby,
verses.tsw_comparator: “When they sin against you—for there is no human being who does not sin—and you become angry with them and give them before an enemy, and their captors carry them captive to a land far or near,

verses.rationale: Keep the threefold confession and return of heart.
verses.before: and they bring it back to their heart in the land where they were carried captive and return and plead with you in the land of their captivity, saying, ‘We have sinned, we have acted perversely, and we have acted wickedly,’
verses.after: if they take it to heart in the land where they are captives, turn back, and plead with you there, saying, ‘We have sinned, done wrong, and acted wickedly,’
verses.tsw_comparator: and they bring it back to their heart in the land where they were carried captive and return and plead with you in the land of their captivity, saying, ‘We have sinned, we have acted perversely, and we have acted wickedly,’

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated captivity and threefold orientation of prayer.
verses.before: and they return to you with all their heart and with all their life in the land of their captivity where they carried them captive, and pray toward their land that you gave to their ancestors, the city that you chose, and the house that I built for your name,
verses.after: if they return to you with all their heart and all their being in the land of their captivity, where they have been taken, and pray toward the land you gave their ancestors, the city you chose, and the house I built for your name,
verses.tsw_comparator: and they return to you with all their heart and with all their life in the land of their captivity where they carried them captive, and pray toward their land that you gave to their ancestors, the city that you chose, and the house that I built for your name,

verses.rationale: Preserve justice and forgiveness as separate requests.
verses.before: then hear from the heavens, from your dwelling place, their prayer and their pleas, maintain their cause, and forgive your people who sinned against you.
verses.after: hear their prayer and pleas from heaven, your settled dwelling place. Uphold their cause, and forgive your people who have sinned against you.
verses.tsw_comparator: then hear from the heavens, from your dwelling place, their prayer and their pleas, maintain their cause, and forgive your people who sinned against you.

verses.rationale: Keep eyes and ears as the closing appeal begins.
verses.before: “And now, my God, please let your eyes be open and your ears attentive to the prayer of this place.
verses.after: “Now, my God, please open your eyes and let your ears attend to the prayer offered in this place.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And now, my God, please let your eyes be open and your ears attentive to the prayer of this place.

verses.rationale: Preserve all four poetic movements and salvation as clothing.
verses.before: And now arise, O LORD God, to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength. Let your priests, O LORD God, be clothed with salvation, and let your faithful ones rejoice in goodness.
verses.after: Now rise, LORD God, to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength. May your priests, LORD God, be clothed with salvation; may your faithful ones rejoice in goodness.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now arise, O LORD God, to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength. Let your priests, O LORD God, be clothed with salvation, and let your faithful ones rejoice in goodness.

verses.rationale: Choose love shown to David while noting the alternative direction.
verses.before: O LORD God, do not turn away the face of your anointed one. Remember the steadfast love of David your servant.”
verses.after: LORD God, do not turn away your anointed one. Remember the faithful love shown to David your servant.”
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD God, do not turn away the face of your anointed one. Remember the steadfast love of David your servant.”

verses.rationale: Keep the separate fire and glory actions.
verses.before: When Solomon had finished praying, fire came down from the heavens and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the house.
verses.after: When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and sacrifices. The LORD’s glory filled the house.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Solomon had finished praying, fire came down from the heavens and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the house.

verses.rationale: Retain the impediment caused by the glory.
verses.before: The priests were not able to enter the house of the LORD because the glory of the LORD had filled the LORD’s house.
verses.after: The priests could not enter the LORD’s house because the LORD’s glory had filled it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priests were not able to enter the house of the LORD because the glory of the LORD had filled the LORD’s house.

verses.rationale: Keep bodily worship and the recurring thanksgiving refrain.
verses.before: When all the children of Israel saw the fire come down and the glory of the LORD upon the house, they bowed with their faces to the ground upon the pavement, worshiped, and gave thanks to the LORD: “For he is good, for his steadfast love is forever.”
verses.after: All the Israelites saw the fire descend and the LORD’s glory over the house. They knelt with their faces to the ground on the pavement, bowed in worship, and thanked the LORD: “For he is good; his faithful love lasts forever.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When all the children of Israel saw the fire come down and the glory of the LORD upon the house, they bowed with their faces to the ground upon the pavement, worshiped, and gave thanks to the LORD: “For he is good, for his steadfast love is forever.”

verses.rationale: Retain the common action of king and people.
verses.before: Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the LORD.
verses.after: The king and all the people offered sacrifices before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserve both large counts and the collective dedication.
verses.before: King Solomon offered a sacrifice of twenty-two thousand cattle and one hundred twenty thousand sheep. Thus the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.
verses.after: King Solomon sacrificed twenty-two thousand cattle and a hundred twenty thousand sheep and goats. In this way the king and all the people dedicated God’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: King Solomon offered a sacrifice of twenty-two thousand cattle and one hundred twenty thousand sheep. Thus the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.

verses.rationale: Keep David’s mediated praise and the two groups’ arrangement.
verses.before: The priests stood at their posts, and the Levites with the instruments of music to the LORD that King David had made for giving thanks to the LORD—“for his steadfast love is forever”—when David praised by their hand. The priests sounded trumpets opposite them, and all Israel stood.
verses.after: The priests stood at their posts. The Levites had the musical instruments for the LORD that King David had made for giving thanks to the LORD—“His faithful love lasts forever”—as David offered praise through them. Opposite them the priests sounded trumpets, and all Israel stood.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priests stood at their posts, and the Levites with the instruments of music to the LORD that King David had made for giving thanks to the LORD—“for his steadfast love is forever”—when David praised by their hand. The priests sounded trumpets opposite them, and all Israel stood.

verses.rationale: Preserve the practical reason and distinguish the offering types.
verses.before: Solomon consecrated the middle of the court that was before the house of the LORD, for there he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the offerings of well-being, because the bronze altar that Solomon had made was not able to contain the burnt offering, the grain offering, and the fat.
verses.after: Solomon consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of the LORD’s house. He offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the well-being offerings there, because the bronze altar he had made could not hold the burnt offering, grain offering, and fat.
verses.tsw_comparator: Solomon consecrated the middle of the court that was before the house of the LORD, for there he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the offerings of well-being, because the bronze altar that Solomon had made was not able to contain the burnt offering, the grain offering, and the fat.

verses.rationale: Retain the week and geographic limits.
verses.before: At that time Solomon made the festival seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great assembly, from Lebo-Hamath to the Wadi of Egypt.
verses.after: At that time Solomon kept the festival for seven days, with all Israel—a very large assembly from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time Solomon made the festival seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great assembly, from Lebo-Hamath to the Wadi of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keep both seven-day periods rather than collapsing them.
verses.before: On the eighth day they held a solemn assembly, for they had made the dedication of the altar seven days and the festival seven days.
verses.after: On the eighth day they held a solemn assembly. They had spent seven days dedicating the altar and seven days celebrating the festival.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the eighth day they held a solemn assembly, for they had made the dedication of the altar seven days and the festival seven days.

verses.rationale: Preserve Chronicles’ date and all three beneficiaries.
verses.before: On the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their tents, joyful and glad of heart because of the good that the LORD had done for David, for Solomon, and for Israel his people.
verses.after: On the twenty-third day of the seventh month, he sent the people to their tents. They went with joyful, glad hearts because of the good the LORD had done for David, Solomon, and his people Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their tents, joyful and glad of heart because of the good that the LORD had done for David, for Solomon, and for Israel his people.

verses.rationale: Keep paired houses and the comprehensive completion statement.
verses.before: So Solomon finished the house of the LORD and the king’s house. All that had come into Solomon’s heart to do in the house of the LORD and in his own house he accomplished successfully.
verses.after: Solomon completed the LORD’s house and the royal house. Everything he had set his heart on doing in the LORD’s house and his own house succeeded.

verses.tsw_comparator: He brought into the house of God the holy things of his father and his own holy things: silver, gold, and vessels.

verses.rationale: Retain the difficult date without silently correcting it.
verses.before: There was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s reign.
verses.after: There was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s reign.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s reign.

verses.rationale: Preserve the source date and blockade’s purpose.
verses.before: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s reign, Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and built Ramah, so that no one could go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
verses.after: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s reign, Baasha king of Israel marched against Judah. He fortified Ramah to prevent anyone from going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s reign, Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and built Ramah, so that no one could go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.

verses.rationale: Keep both treasuries and the named recipient.

verses.after: Asa brought silver and gold out of the treasuries of the LORD’s house and the royal house and sent it to Ben-hadad king of Aram, who lived in Damascus, with this message:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Asa brought out silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the king’s house and sent them to Ben-Hadad king of Aram, who lived in Damascus, saying,

verses.rationale: Retain covenant repetition and the proposed breach.
verses.before: “There is a covenant between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. Look, I am sending you silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me.”

verses.tsw_comparator: “There is a covenant between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. Look, I am sending you silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me.”

verses.rationale: Keep Chronicles’ Abel-maim and storage wording.
verses.before: Ben-Hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel. They struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-Maim, and all the storage cities of Naphtali.
verses.after: Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent his army commanders against Israel’s towns. They struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the storage places of Naphtali’s towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ben-Hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel. They struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-Maim, and all the storage cities of Naphtali.

verses.rationale: Preserve the military effect of the attack.
verses.before: When Baasha heard of it, he stopped building Ramah and ceased his work.
verses.after: When Baasha heard, he stopped fortifying Ramah and abandoned his work.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Baasha heard of it, he stopped building Ramah and ceased his work.

verses.rationale: Keep reused materials and both destination towns.
verses.before: Then King Asa took all Judah, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and its timber with which Baasha had been building. With them he built Geba and Mizpah.
verses.after: King Asa brought all Judah to carry away the stones and timber Baasha had used at Ramah. With them he built Geba and Mizpah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then King Asa took all Judah, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and its timber with which Baasha had been building. With them he built Geba and Mizpah.

verses.rationale: Retain Aram as the escaped army rather than substituting Israel.
verses.before: At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, “Because you relied upon the king of Aram and did not rely upon the LORD your God, therefore the army of the king of Aram has escaped from your hand.
verses.after: At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said, “Because you relied on the king of Aram instead of relying on the LORD your God, the army of the king of Aram has escaped your hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, “Because you relied upon the king of Aram and did not rely upon the LORD your God, therefore the army of the king of Aram has escaped from your hand.

verses.rationale: Keep the two named peoples and repeated reliance.
verses.before: Were not the Cushites and Libyans a very great army, with chariots and horsemen in great abundance? Yet because you relied upon the LORD, he gave them into your hand.
verses.after: Were not the Cushites and Libyans a vast army, with great numbers of chariots and horsemen? Yet when you relied on the LORD, he handed them over to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Were not the Cushites and Libyans a very great army, with chariots and horsemen in great abundance? Yet because you relied upon the LORD, he gave them into your hand.

verses.rationale: Retain roaming eyes, whole hearts and the adverse future.
verses.before: For the eyes of the LORD range throughout all the earth to show himself strong for those whose heart is whole toward him. You have acted foolishly in this, for from now on you will have wars.”
verses.after: The LORD’s eyes range throughout the earth to show his strength for those whose hearts are whole toward him. You have acted foolishly in this. From now on, you will have wars.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For the eyes of the LORD range throughout all the earth to show himself strong for those whose heart is whole toward him. You have acted foolishly in this, for from now on you will have wars.”

verses.rationale: Keep both the prophet’s confinement and wider oppression explicit.
verses.before: Then Asa became angry with the seer and put him in the house of the stocks, for he was enraged with him because of this. Asa oppressed some of the people at that time.
verses.after: Asa was angry with the seer and put him in prison, in stocks, furious at what he had said. At that time Asa also brutally oppressed some of the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Asa became angry with the seer and put him in the house of the stocks, for he was enraged with him because of this. Asa oppressed some of the people at that time.

verses.rationale: Preserve the source’s record title and order.
verses.before: And look, the acts of Asa, first and last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.after: Asa’s acts, from first to last, are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: And look, the acts of Asa, first and last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

verses.rationale: Retain the contrast as a narrative judgment without a general medical prohibition.
verses.before: In the thirty-ninth year of his reign Asa became diseased in his feet, and his disease became very severe. Yet even in his disease he did not seek the LORD but the physicians.
verses.after: In the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa became diseased in his feet, and his illness grew severe. Even in his illness he did not seek the LORD, but sought the physicians.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the thirty-ninth year of his reign Asa became diseased in his feet, and his disease became very severe. Yet even in his disease he did not seek the LORD but the physicians.

verses.rationale: Keep both death expressions and the precise year.
verses.before: Asa lay down with his ancestors and died in the forty-first year of his reign.
verses.after: Asa lay down with his ancestors. He died in the forty-first year of his reign.
verses.tsw_comparator: Asa lay down with his ancestors and died in the forty-first year of his reign.

verses.rationale: Distinguish burial from the honorary burning rather than implying cremation.
verses.before: They buried him in his own tomb that he had cut for himself in the city of David. They laid him on a bier filled with spices and various blended ointments, and they made a very great burning for him.
verses.after: They buried him in the tomb he had cut for himself in David’s City. They laid him on a bier filled with spices and various preparations blended by a perfumer’s skill, and made an exceptionally great fire in his honor.
verses.tsw_comparator: They buried him in his own tomb that he had cut for himself in the city of David. They laid him on a bier filled with spices and various blended ointments, and they made a very great burning for him.

verses.rationale: Keep succession and the northern threat distinct.
verses.before: Jehoshaphat his son became king in his place and strengthened himself against Israel.
verses.after: His son Jehoshaphat became king in his place and strengthened his position against Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoshaphat his son became king in his place and strengthened himself against Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserve both territories and their prior capture.
verses.before: He placed forces in all the fortified cities of Judah and put garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that Asa his father had captured.
verses.after: He stationed troops in all Judah’s fortified towns and placed garrisons throughout Judah and in the towns of Ephraim his father Asa had captured.
verses.tsw_comparator: He placed forces in all the fortified cities of Judah and put garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that Asa his father had captured.

verses.rationale: Retain David and the earlier-ways qualification.
verses.before: The LORD was with Jehoshaphat because he walked in the earlier ways of David his ancestor and did not seek the Baals,
verses.after: The LORD was with Jehoshaphat because he walked in the earlier ways of his ancestor David and did not seek the Baals.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD was with Jehoshaphat because he walked in the earlier ways of David his ancestor and did not seek the Baals,

verses.rationale: Keep the contrast in seeking and conduct.
verses.before: but sought the God of his father and walked in his commandments and not according to the acts of Israel.
verses.after: Instead, he sought his father’s God and followed his commands, unlike Israel’s practices.
verses.tsw_comparator: but sought the God of his father and walked in his commandments and not according to the acts of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserve divine establishment and the source of tribute.
verses.before: So the LORD established the kingdom in his hand, and all Judah brought tribute to Jehoshaphat. He had riches and honor in abundance.
verses.after: The LORD established the kingdom in his hand. All Judah brought tribute to Jehoshaphat, and he had great wealth and honor.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the LORD established the kingdom in his hand, and all Judah brought tribute to Jehoshaphat. He had riches and honor in abundance.

verses.rationale: Choose positive courage for the lifted-heart image in this context.
verses.before: His heart was courageous in the ways of the LORD, and he further removed the high places and the Asherah poles from Judah.
verses.after: His heart took courage in the LORD’s ways. He also removed the high places and Asherah poles from Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: His heart was courageous in the ways of the LORD, and he further removed the high places and the Asherah poles from Judah.

verses.rationale: Keep every official and the year of the teaching mission.
verses.before: In the third year of his reign he sent his officials Ben-Hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah to teach in the cities of Judah.
verses.after: In the third year of his reign he sent his officials Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah to teach in Judah’s towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the third year of his reign he sent his officials Ben-Hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah to teach in the cities of Judah.

verses.rationale: Preserve the full roster and distinguish Levites from priests.
verses.before: With them were Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-Adonijah; and with these Levites were Elishama and Jehoram the priests.
verses.after: With them went the Levites Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-adonijah, and the priests Elishama and Jehoram.
verses.tsw_comparator: With them were Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-Adonijah; and with these Levites were Elishama and Jehoram the priests.

verses.rationale: Keep the book and repeated scope of teaching.
verses.before: They taught in Judah, having with them the book of the instruction of the LORD. They went around throughout all the cities of Judah and taught among the people.
verses.after: They taught throughout Judah, carrying the Book of the LORD’s Instruction. They traveled through every town in Judah and taught the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: They taught in Judah, having with them the book of the instruction of the LORD. They went around throughout all the cities of Judah and taught among the people.

verses.rationale: Preserve the stated relation between dread and peace.
verses.before: The fear of the LORD fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that were around Judah, and they did not make war against Jehoshaphat.
verses.after: Dread of the LORD fell on all the kingdoms surrounding Judah, and they did not go to war with Jehoshaphat.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fear of the LORD fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that were around Judah, and they did not make war against Jehoshaphat.

verses.rationale: Keep the distinct peoples and both equal totals.
verses.before: Some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat gifts and silver as tribute, and the Arabians also brought him flocks: seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred male goats.
verses.after: Some Philistines brought Jehoshaphat gifts and silver as tribute. The Arabs also brought him flocks: seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred male goats.
verses.tsw_comparator: Some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat gifts and silver as tribute, and the Arabians also brought him flocks: seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred male goats.

verses.rationale: Retain progressive growth and both building types.
verses.before: Jehoshaphat grew greater and greater. He built fortresses and storage cities in Judah.
verses.after: Jehoshaphat grew greater and greater. He built fortresses and storage towns in Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoshaphat grew greater and greater. He built fortresses and storage cities in Judah.

verses.rationale: Keep work and warriors separate rather than inserting supplies.
verses.before: He had much work in the cities of Judah, and men of war, mighty warriors, in Jerusalem.
verses.after: He had extensive work in Judah’s towns, and capable fighting men in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: He had much work in the cities of Judah, and men of war, mighty warriors, in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Introduce the roster and retain the first total.
verses.before: This was their enrollment according to their ancestral houses: from Judah, commanders of thousands—Adnah the commander, and with him three hundred thousand mighty warriors;
verses.after: These were their enrolled numbers by ancestral house. From Judah, the commanders of thousands were: Adnah the commander, with three hundred thousand capable warriors;
verses.tsw_comparator: This was their enrollment according to their ancestral houses: from Judah, commanders of thousands—Adnah the commander, and with him three hundred thousand mighty warriors;

verses.rationale: Keep the second commander and number.
verses.before: next to him Jehohanan the commander, and with him two hundred eighty thousand;
verses.after: next to him, Jehohanan the commander, with two hundred eighty thousand;
verses.tsw_comparator: next to him Jehohanan the commander, and with him two hundred eighty thousand;

verses.rationale: Retain the unusual volunteer description.
verses.before: next to him Amasiah son of Zichri, who willingly offered himself to the LORD, and with him two hundred thousand mighty warriors.
verses.after: and next to him, Amasiah son of Zichri, who volunteered for the LORD, with two hundred thousand capable warriors.
verses.tsw_comparator: next to him Amasiah son of Zichri, who willingly offered himself to the LORD, and with him two hundred thousand mighty warriors.

verses.rationale: Keep tribe, commander, number and equipment.
verses.before: From Benjamin: Eliada, a mighty warrior, and with him two hundred thousand armed with bow and shield;
verses.after: From Benjamin: Eliada, a capable warrior, with two hundred thousand men armed with bows and shields;
verses.tsw_comparator: From Benjamin: Eliada, a mighty warrior, and with him two hundred thousand armed with bow and shield;

verses.rationale: Retain the last commander and troop total.
verses.before: next to him Jehozabad, and with him one hundred eighty thousand equipped for war.
verses.after: and next to him, Jehozabad, with a hundred eighty thousand equipped for military service.
verses.tsw_comparator: next to him Jehozabad, and with him one hundred eighty thousand equipped for war.

verses.rationale: Keep the listed forces additional to the garrisons.
verses.before: These served the king besides those whom the king had put in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.
verses.after: These served the king, besides those he had stationed in fortified towns throughout Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: These served the king besides those whom the king had put in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.

verses.rationale: Preserve the family basis of the alliance.
verses.before: Jehoshaphat had riches and honor in abundance, and he allied himself by marriage with Ahab.
verses.after: Jehoshaphat had great wealth and honor, and he formed a marriage alliance with Ahab.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoshaphat had riches and honor in abundance, and he allied himself by marriage with Ahab.

verses.rationale: Keep hospitality and inducement together.
verses.before: After some years he went down to Ahab at Samaria. Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle in abundance for him and for the people who were with him and persuaded him to go up against Ramoth-Gilead.
verses.after: Some years later he went down to Ahab in Samaria. Ahab slaughtered many sheep, goats, and cattle for him and the people with him, and urged him to march against Ramoth-gilead.
verses.tsw_comparator: After some years he went down to Ahab at Samaria. Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle in abundance for him and for the people who were with him and persuaded him to go up against Ramoth-Gilead.

verses.rationale: Retain the solidarity formula and military commitment.
verses.before: Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, “Will you go with me to Ramoth-Gilead?” He said to him, “I am as you are, and my people as your people; we will be with you in the war.”
verses.after: Ahab king of Israel asked Jehoshaphat king of Judah, “Will you go with me to Ramoth-gilead?” He answered, “I am as you are, and my people are as your people. I will be with you in the war.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, “Will you go with me to Ramoth-Gilead?” He said to him, “I am as you are, and my people as your people; we will be with you in the war.”

verses.rationale: Make the requested inquiry precede action.
verses.before: Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, “Please inquire today for the word of the LORD.”
verses.after: But Jehoshaphat said to Israel’s king, “Please inquire first for the LORD’s word.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, “Please inquire today for the word of the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the number and the question’s plural-to-singular shift.
verses.before: So the king of Israel gathered the prophets, four hundred men, and said to them, “Will we go against Ramoth-Gilead for battle, or will I refrain?” They said, “Go up, for God will give it into the hand of the king.”
verses.after: Israel’s king gathered four hundred prophets and asked, “Should we go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or should I hold back?” They answered, “Go up! God will hand it over to the king.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So the king of Israel gathered the prophets, four hundred men, and said to them, “Shall we go against Ramoth-Gilead for battle, or shall I refrain?” They said, “Go up, for God will give it into the hand of the king.”

verses.rationale: Keep another prophet rather than declaring the four hundred’s status.
verses.before: Yet Jehoshaphat said, “Is there not still a prophet of the LORD here, so that we may inquire through him?”
verses.after: Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there not another prophet of the LORD here whom we can consult?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jehoshaphat said, “Is there not still a prophet of the LORD here, so that we may inquire through him?”

verses.rationale: Keep Ahab’s grievance as his own assertion.
verses.before: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “There is still one man through whom we may inquire of the LORD, but I hate him, for he never prophesies good concerning me, but always evil. He is Micaiah son of Imlah.” Jehoshaphat said, “Let not the king say so.”
verses.after: Israel’s king told him, “There is still one man through whom we can inquire of the LORD, but I hate him. He never prophesies good for me; all his days it is disaster. He is Micaiah son of Imlah.” Jehoshaphat replied, “The king should not say that.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “There is still one man through whom we may inquire of the LORD, but I hate him, for he never prophesies good concerning me, but always evil. He is Micaiah son of Imlah.” Jehoshaphat said, “Let not the king say so.”

verses.rationale: Render the court role while noting the possible eunuch sense.
verses.before: Then the king of Israel called one court official and said, “Bring quickly Micaiah son of Imlah.”
verses.after: Israel’s king called an officer and said, “Bring Micaiah son of Imlah quickly.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king of Israel called one court official and said, “Bring quickly Micaiah son of Imlah.”

verses.rationale: Retain the earthly throne scene and location.
verses.before: Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting each on his throne, clothed in their robes, sitting at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
verses.after: Israel’s king and Jehoshaphat king of Judah sat in their robes, each on his throne, at the threshing floor by Samaria’s gate. All the prophets were prophesying before them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting each on his throne, clothed in their robes, sitting at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.

verses.rationale: Preserve the enacted violent image and claimed divine speech.
verses.before: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made for himself horns of iron and said, “Thus says the LORD: With these you will gore Aram until you have finished them.”
verses.after: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made iron horns and said, “The LORD says: With these you will gore the Arameans until you destroy them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made for himself horns of iron and said, “Thus says the LORD: With these you shall gore Aram until you have finished them.”

verses.rationale: Keep unanimity and the repeated promise.
verses.before: All the prophets prophesied likewise, saying, “Go up to Ramoth-Gilead and succeed, for the LORD will give it into the hand of the king.”
verses.after: All the prophets prophesied the same: “March against Ramoth-gilead and succeed! The LORD will hand it over to the king.”
verses.tsw_comparator: All the prophets prophesied likewise, saying, “Go up to Ramoth-Gilead and succeed, for the LORD will give it into the hand of the king.”

verses.rationale: Retain the pressure to conform and one-voice image.
verses.before: The messenger who had gone to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, “Look, the words of the prophets are with one mouth good toward the king. Please let your word be like one of theirs and speak good.”
verses.after: The messenger sent to summon Micaiah told him, “Look, the prophets speak with one voice in the king’s favor. Please let your word agree with theirs. Speak favorably.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The messenger who had gone to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, “Look, the words of the prophets are with one mouth good toward the king. Please let your word be like one of theirs and speak good.”

verses.rationale: Keep the oath and restriction on his speech.
verses.before: Yet Micaiah said, “As the LORD lives, whatever my God says, that I will speak.”
verses.after: Micaiah answered, “As the LORD lives, I will speak whatever my God says.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Micaiah said, “As the LORD lives, whatever my God says, that I will speak.”

verses.rationale: Retain the initial favorable answer without inserting a sarcastic stage direction.
verses.before: He came to the king, and the king said to him, “Micaiah, will we go to Ramoth-Gilead for battle, or will I refrain?” He said, “Go up and succeed, and they will be given into your hand.”
verses.after: When he came to the king, the king asked, “Micaiah, should we go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or should I hold back?” He replied, “Go up and succeed! They will be handed over to you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He came to the king, and the king said to him, “Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth-Gilead for battle, or shall I refrain?” He said, “Go up and succeed, and they will be given into your hand.”

verses.rationale: Keep the oath-demand and truth criterion.
verses.before: The king said to him, “How many times must I put you under oath that you speak to me nothing but truth in the name of the LORD?”
verses.after: The king said, “How many times must I put you under oath to tell me nothing but the truth in the LORD’s name?”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king said to him, “How many times must I put you under oath that you speak to me nothing but truth in the name of the LORD?”

verses.rationale: Retain the shepherd image and distinct peace outcome for the people.
verses.before: Then he said: “I saw all Israel scattered upon the mountains like sheep without a shepherd. And the LORD said, ‘These have no master. Let each return to his house in peace.’”
verses.after: Then Micaiah said, “I saw all Israel scattered over the mountains like sheep without a shepherd. The LORD said, ‘These have no master. Let each go home in peace.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said: “I saw all Israel scattered upon the mountains like sheep without a shepherd. And the LORD said, ‘These have no master. Let each return to his house in peace.’”

verses.rationale: Keep the king’s repeated complaint.
verses.before: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?”
verses.after: Israel’s king said to Jehoshaphat, “Did I not tell you? He prophesies nothing good for me, only disaster.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?”

verses.rationale: Preserve the heavenly throne scene’s correspondence with verse 9.
verses.before: Micaiah said, “Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting upon his throne, and all the host of the heavens standing on his right and on his left.
verses.after: Micaiah continued, “Then hear the LORD’s word. I saw the LORD seated on his throne, with all heaven’s army standing to his right and left.
verses.tsw_comparator: Micaiah said, “Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting upon his throne, and all the host of the heavens standing on his right and on his left.

verses.rationale: Keep the divine question’s lethal purpose explicit.
verses.before: The LORD said, ‘Who will entice Ahab king of Israel so that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-Gilead?’ One said this, and another said that.
verses.after: The LORD asked, ‘Who will entice Ahab king of Israel to march up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?’ One said this, another said that.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said, ‘Who will entice Ahab king of Israel so that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-Gilead?’ One said this, and another said that.

verses.rationale: Retain the definite spirit without assigning a name.
verses.before: Then a spirit came forward and stood before the LORD and said, ‘I will entice him.’ The LORD said to him, ‘By what?’
verses.after: Then the spirit came forward, stood before the LORD, and said, ‘I will entice him.’ The LORD asked, ‘How?’
verses.tsw_comparator: Then a spirit came forward and stood before the LORD and said, ‘I will entice him.’ The LORD said to him, ‘By what?’

verses.rationale: Preserve the commissioned deception without doctrinal explanation.

verses.after: Whenever a dispute comes to you from your fellow Israelites living in their towns—whether a case of bloodshed or a question about instruction, commandment, statutes, or judgments—you must warn them, so they do not incur guilt before the LORD and bring wrath upon you and your people. verses.rationale: Keep differentiated responsibilities and the closing wish.

verses.rationale: Retain all three instruments and destination.
verses.before: They came to Jerusalem with harps, lyres, and trumpets, to the house of the LORD.
verses.after: They entered Jerusalem with harps, lyres, and trumpets and went to the LORD’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: They came to Jerusalem with harps, lyres, and trumpets, to the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keep the widening response and divine warfare claim.
verses.before: The fear of God was upon all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that the LORD had fought against the enemies of Israel.
verses.after: Dread of God fell on all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that the LORD had fought against Israel’s enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fear of God was upon all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that the LORD had fought against the enemies of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserve quiet and surrounding rest as a narrative close.
verses.before: So the kingdom of Jehoshaphat had rest, and his God gave him rest all around.
verses.after: Jehoshaphat’s kingdom was quiet, for his God had given him rest on every side.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the kingdom of Jehoshaphat had rest, and his God gave him rest all around.

verses.rationale: Keep age, reign length and maternal ancestry.
verses.before: Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
verses.after: Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five when he became king and reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

verses.rationale: Retain the positive evaluation before its qualification.
verses.before: He walked in the way of Asa his father and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.after: He followed the way of his father Asa without turning aside, doing what was right in the LORD’s eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: He walked in the way of Asa his father and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keep the unresolved qualification despite earlier removals.
verses.before: Only the high places were not removed, and the people had not yet set their heart toward the God of their ancestors.
verses.after: Yet the high places remained, and the people still had not set their hearts on their ancestors’ God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only the high places were not removed, and the people had not yet set their heart toward the God of their ancestors.

verses.rationale: Preserve the nested source attribution.
verses.before: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, first and last, look, they are written in the words of Jehu son of Hanani, which were included in the book of the kings of Israel.
verses.after: Jehoshaphat’s remaining acts, from first to last, are written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani, which were included in the Book of the Kings of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, first and last, look, they are written in the words of Jehu son of Hanani, which were included in the book of the kings of Israel.

verses.rationale: Choose Ahaziah as the final clause’s referent while noting possible ambiguity.
verses.before: After this Jehoshaphat king of Judah joined himself with Ahaziah king of Israel, who acted wickedly.
verses.after: After this, Jehoshaphat king of Judah joined with Ahaziah king of Israel, who acted wickedly.
verses.tsw_comparator: After this Jehoshaphat king of Judah joined himself with Ahaziah king of Israel, who acted wickedly.

verses.rationale: Retain Tarshish as stated destination without harmonizing Kings.
verses.before: He joined with him to make ships to go to Tarshish, and they made the ships at Ezion-Geber.
verses.after: He joined with him to make ships to sail to Tarshish. They built the ships at Ezion-geber.
verses.tsw_comparator: He joined with him to make ships to go to Tarshish, and they made the ships at Ezion-Geber.

verses.rationale: Keep the prophet’s full name and the shared shattering image.
verses.before: Then Eliezer son of Dodavahu from Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, “Because you joined yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD has broken your works.” So the ships were wrecked and were not able to go to Tarshish.
verses.after: Eliezer son of Dodavahu from Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat: “Because you joined with Ahaziah, the LORD has shattered your work.” The ships broke up and could not sail to Tarshish.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Eliezer son of Dodavahu from Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, “Because you joined yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD has broken your works.” So the ships were wrecked and were not able to go to Tarshish.
